summary: Initializes a UI edit-box-like object to default state with no branches. Clears the string buffer (first byte of *(this+0x2F0) set to 0), points the cursor/position pointer at this+0x2F4 to the buffer start, sets buffer size this+0x2F8 to 256 and char limit this+0x300 to 16, zeroes length/counter this+0x2E8, and writes a fixed set of byte flags at this+0xE0..0xE5, this+0x1E7 and this+0x2EC (mix of 0/1, mostly enabled). Always returns 0.

operations.description: Zero the first byte of the string buffer pointed to by field this+0x2F0: **(_BYTE **)(this+752) = 0 (empty string).
Set field this+0x2F4 (cursor/current-position pointer) to the value of field this+0x2F0 (buffer start).
Zero byte flag at field this+0x1E7 (alternate string buffer first byte / behavior flag).
Set byte flags at fields this+0xE0 and this+0xE2 to 0 (display/behavior options).
Set byte flags at fields this+0xE3, this+0xE4 and this+0xE1 to 1 (enabled options).
Set byte flag at field this+0xE5 to 0 (behavior option).
Set byte flag at field this+0x2EC to 1.
Set field this+0x300 (char limit / max input length) to 16.
Return 0 (result initialized to 0 before the writes).

unresolved: Exact meaning of the individual byte flags at this+0xE0..0xE5, this+0x1E7 and this+0x2EC (display, selection, enabled, behavior options) is inferred from the edit-box interpretation in existing analysis.
Purpose of the cursor pointer at this+0x2F4 vs. the buffer pointer at this+0x2F0.
Whether this+0x2E8 is a character count/length field.
